stimulus: HearthLink — a proprietary smart-home hub, sold at a subsidized upfront price, that controls your lights, locks, and thermostat from one app. After two years on the market, continued use of your existing automations starts requiring a mandatory $10/month subscription.
custom_segment_description: US suburban homeowners 30-55 who adopted early smart-home devices

outcome.label: flop
outcome.evidence: publicly-known pattern of smart-home hub makers retroactively imposing a mandatory subscription on already-purchased hardware to keep existing automations working, triggering public backlash, mass customer abandonment, and in some documented cases a full shutdown of the hub's cloud service.

provenance.disguise_notes: no specific brand or company named; value prop (subsidized proprietary hub, later gated behind a retroactive mandatory subscription) and audience preserved from the publicly-known pattern
